subject.title: Auto-apply safe doctor fixes on gateway start

question: Should Gateway startup ever mutate persisted config by running a safe doctor repair subset, and what surfaces must be excluded or explicitly opted in?
rationale: The central behavior is not a missing mechanical call; unattended repair crosses config, plugin, channel, auth/provider, and sandbox boundaries where the safe default needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Define an allowlisted startup repair subset
options.body: Create a narrow audited set of non-destructive startup repairs with explicit exclusions for sandbox, auth/provider, plugin disablement, and channel availability changes before implementation.

options.title: Keep startup manual-only
options.body: Preserve the current fail-with-doctor-guidance behavior and rely on `openclaw doctor --fix` or supervisor preflight scripts for operators who want automatic repair.

options.title: Add an explicit broad opt-in
options.body: Introduce a documented `doctor.autoFix` or equivalent config policy, accepting the compatibility and security review burden for existing upgrades and unattended writes.

recommendation.title: Define an allowlisted startup repair subset
recommendation.body: Create a narrow audited set of non-destructive startup repairs with explicit exclusions for sandbox, auth/provider, plugin disablement, and channel availability changes before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current central-file blame and adjacent config/security policy history make this the best available routing candidate for the startup repair boundary decision.
